hero.lede: A 40,000 m² commercial property in Stora Essingen. Open-plan offices with a ceiling that needed to absorb sound — without calling attention to itself.

brief.body_p1: The building management wanted a ceiling solution that would improve speech intelligibility across the open floor. The space was a standard suspended T-grid layout — fast to install, but acoustically untreated.
brief.body_p2: The requirement was speech intelligibility across an open floor, and a ceiling that reads as a neutral surface rather than as acoustic treatment. Absorption had to do its work between 500 Hz and 2 kHz, where conversation sits.
brief.body_p3: Aisti Aalto went up alongside the standard mineral wool tile in the same grid, in the same 600 × 600 module, so the two could be compared in place.

results.note: Absorption coefficients from Aisti's EN ISO 354 reverberation room test, 20 mm mounted tight to the soffit. In that build-up Aisti rate the tile αw 0.65 — Class C to EN ISO 11654 — because absorption at 125 Hz falls to 0.10 and the single-number rating follows the weak end. Across 500 Hz to 2 kHz it holds 0.75 to 0.80. The same tile over a 200 mm plenum is rated αw 0.95, Class A.
